title: Integral pushforward identifies the two test-base comparison arrows
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $p:X\to S$ and $g:T\to S$ morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and $\pi:T'\to T$ an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Put $g'=g\circ\pi$. Form $Y=X\times_ST$ with projections $e:Y\to T$, $h:Y\to X$, and $Y'=X\times_ST'$ with projections $e':Y'\to T'$, $h':Y'\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $M$ be any sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $T'_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and $r\in\mathbf Z$. For the direct and inverse images of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] there are natural isomorphisms
$$A_M:p^{-1}R^rg_*(\pi_*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}p^{-1}R^rg'_*M,\qquad B_M:R^rh_*e^{-1}(\pi_*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R^rh'_*e'^{-1}M.$$
If $b_{\pi_*M}$ and $b'_M$ denote the canonical degree-$r$ base-change maps of the two squares [sk-def-bc], these isomorphisms satisfy
$$B_M\circ b_{\pi_*M}=b'_M\circ A_M.$$
There is no surjectivity condition on $\pi$ and no lower-degree base-change hypothesis.

proof.text: Let $k:Y'\to Y$ be the unique morphism with $e\circ k=\pi\circ e'$ and $h\circ k=h'$, obtained from the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Its square with $\pi$, $e$, $e'$ is Cartesian: a pair of maps to $Y$ and $T'$ with the same map to $T$ gives maps to $X$ and $T'$ with the same map to $S$, hence a unique map to $Y'$; both constructions are inverse by uniqueness. Thus [lem-sbc-integral-morphism-base-change] makes $k$ integral. In particular $g'=g\circ\pi$ and $h'=h\circ k$ give a vertical paste of the exchanged squares.

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-integral-etale-direct-image-exact], $\pi_*$ and $k_*$ are exact on abelian etale sheaves. They are also exact on $\Lambda$-module sheaves: forgetting scalars is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients], their underlying direct images are the abelian ones by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and kernels, images and cokernels have their induced module structures, so an underlying exact sequence is exact as a module sequence. Also every inverse image here is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor](2) to these exact functors. On bounded-below complexes, $R\pi_*$ and $Rk_*$ are the termwise functors; in particular there is a canonical natural isomorphism $\iota_M:(\pi_*M)[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_*(M[0])$.

source.place: Tag 04C2, lemma-what-integral (4); derived.tex Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor (2),(4); module extension by underlying exact sequences

proof.text: Fix $K\in D^+(T'_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. For the Cartesian square of $k$ over $\pi$, [lem-sbc-integral-underived-exchange] supplies the canonical sheaf-level isomorphism $e^{-1}\pi_*\xrightarrow{\sim}k_*e'^{-1}$ for arbitrary $\Lambda$. Its derived exchange $E:e^{-1}R\pi_*\to Rk_*e'^{-1}$ is also an isomorphism. To verify this for the canonical arrow rather than just its endpoints, first take $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ and a bounded-below K-injective representative $I$ of $K$, followed by a K-injective resolution $j:e'^{-1}I\to J$. The formula [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise](a),(b) represents the derived exchange by the termwise sheaf exchange followed by $k_*j$. The former is a degreewise isomorphism, and the latter a quasi-isomorphism: [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] identifies its cohomology maps with $k_*H^r(j)$ since $k_*$ is exact. Thus the canonical abelian derived exchange is an isomorphism. For arbitrary $\Lambda$, clauses (1)-(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] identify the forgotten canonical derived arrow with precisely this abelian arrow and explicitly reflect its invertibility. Consequently $E_K$ is a natural isomorphism for every $K\in D^+(T'_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$.

proof.text:
Put $K=M[0]$ and $N=(\pi_*M)[0]$. Use the canonical composition isomorphisms $d_{g,\pi}:Rg'_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*R\pi_*$ and $d_{h,k}:Rh'_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*Rk_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], on the constant-ring etale topoi. Define natural isomorphisms in $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ by
$$\alpha=(p^{-1}d_{g,\pi,K}^{-1})\circ p^{-1}Rg_*(\iota_M):p^{-1}Rg_*N\xrightarrow{\sim}p^{-1}Rg'_*K,$$
$$\beta=d_{h,k,e'^{-1}K}^{-1}\circ Rh_*(E_K)\circ Rh_*e^{-1}(\iota_M):Rh_*e^{-1}N\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh'_*e'^{-1}K.$$
These are well defined: all inputs are bounded below (in particular $K$ and $N$ are in degree zero), exact inverse images preserve this property, and the direct images and their composition comparisons restrict to $D^+$. The invertibility of $E_K$ is Step 3; all other factors are functors applied to isomorphisms or canonical composition isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Let $b_C=\operatorname{BC}_{p,g}(C)$ and $b'_K=\operatorname{BC}_{p,g'}(K)$ denote the derived maps of [sbc-def-base-change-map]. Apply the vertical-pasting formula of [sk-lem-pbc-exchange-pasting] with $(f,e,h,f',e',g,g')$ in that node replaced, respectively, by $(\pi,g,p,k,h,e,e')$. In the present notation it says
$$d_{h,k,e'^{-1}K}\circ b'_K=Rh_*(E_K)\circ b_{R\pi_*K}\circ p^{-1}d_{g,\pi,K}.$$
Here each $d$ is the canonical comparison of Step 4, not an arbitrary endpoint isomorphism. Naturality of $b$ for $\iota_M:N\to R\pi_*K$ says
$$b_{R\pi_*K}\circ p^{-1}Rg_*(\iota_M)=Rh_*e^{-1}(\iota_M)\circ b_N.$$
Substituting and multiplying the pasting identity on the left by $d_{h,k,e'^{-1}K}^{-1}$ and on the right by $p^{-1}d_{g,\pi,K}^{-1}\circ p^{-1}Rg_*(\iota_M)$ yields $\beta\circ b_N=b'_K\circ\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 0E46, remark-compose-base-change (vertical composition of the base-change maps constructed in Tag 07A7, remark-base-change); current blueprint sk-lem-pbc-exchange-pasting, second displayed formula; arrow calculation in IntegralBaseChange.lean:105-123

proof.text: Apply $H^r$ to Step 5. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], exactness of $p^{-1}$ identifies $H^r(p^{-1}Rg_*N)$ with $p^{-1}R^rg_*(\pi_*M)$, and similarly for $g'$. The target identifications are $H^r(Rh_*e^{-1}N)=R^rh_*e^{-1}(\pi_*M)$ and $H^r(Rh'_*e'^{-1}K)=R^rh'_*e'^{-1}M$, by the higher-direct-image convention [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and exactness of $e^{-1},e'^{-1}$. Define $A_M=H^r(\alpha)$ and $B_M=H^r(\beta)$ under these identifications. They are natural isomorphisms because cohomology is a functor. By [sbc-def-base-change-map], $H^r(b_N)=b_{\pi_*M}$ and $H^r(b'_K)=b'_M$. Functoriality of $H^r$ gives exactly $B_M\circ b_{\pi_*M}=b'_M\circ A_M$ for every integer $r$. No step used surjectivity, quasi-compactness of $g$, a torsion condition, or any lower-degree base-change assumption.
